# Native developer entry points

Default `make`/`linux-setup`, `make run`/`linux-run`, `make test`/`linux-test`, `linux-test-fast` and `linux-shortcut-test` now use Rust. The source coordinator builds and validates a complete optimized bundle, including resources and workers; launching a bare Cargo executable would not supply the app's required relative runtime layout. Build-only setup removes its temporary package while retaining compiler artifacts. Run owns its private bundle until the native process exits, forwards the next invocation through the existing application identity and cleans up after Quit. Compiler/package diagnostics go to stderr, keeping native command output separate. Existing compiler cancellation and terminal handling remain shared with source installation.

Make defaults `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` to the checkout's `tmp/native-build` and respects an explicit override. No setup/run operation installs to the user's application prefix. The native test gate builds the runtime, runs the workspace suite, applies strict all-target Clippy to default and widget-only configurations, checks formatting and checks generated feature documentation. The fast target selects configuration/transcript, persistence, prompt/draft and Live-policy contracts. Environment-dependent tests remain explicit ignored checks until invoked through their private runners.

Remaining Python tests still protect the implementation and GUI fixtures retained during acceptance. Their existing preparation/full gate are now named `linux-python-setup` and `linux-python-test`; unconverted GUI targets depend on that preparation explicitly. They are still required for handoff and in the on-demand CI job. This is a transition toward complete Python removal, not an exemption from it. CI now requests the Rust application's development libraries and bubblewrap; no hosted job or paid runner was requested, and clean-distribution acceptance is not established by changing its configuration.

## Real Make launch and cleanup

`source_make_build_and_run_without_python` extends the existing process-bootstrap test owner at the public Make boundary. An absolute-path Python trap and a PATH-selected uv trap have positive controls. Actual `make linux-setup` first failed on the previous Makefile with interpreter status 99, reported by Make as exit 2; the intended failure remains in `tmp/native-make-before.log`.

The repaired test builds the actual production bundle and verifies that setup leaves its private home untouched. `make run` starts a resident native process whose executable and Rust payload receipt are observed through the public D-Bus owner PID. Its visible accessibility names/items and complete action description match the unchanged released `normal-hide-reopen` case. A second actual `make run` returns successfully and retains the original application owner. Public Quit terminates the process and Make, removes the temporary runtime, and preserves unrelated user bytes. Neither trap may be used. No production test hook or replacement application implementation is introduced.

The immutable reference remains v1.6.0 at `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f`; existing bootstrap snapshots and expected values are unchanged. The separate resident comparison is repeated against a freshly prepared optimized bundle: 38 public states, thirteen actions, five CLI contracts, forwarding, cold synthetic-PCM Record/quit and three startup faults pass. The new source-entry check does not replace those broader process observations or claim pixel/layout coverage beyond them.

## Native portal command and retired helper

`linux/tests/run_global_shortcut_portal_smoke.sh` now prepares the Rust test dependencies, then runs the existing native [portal comparison](shortcuts-evidence.md) on a new private session bus, with a private HOME/XDG tree, network/PID namespaces and masked devices. It inherits no display or accessibility bus. The old shell runner was independently overlaid inside the private verification namespace: the positively checked uv trap made it exit 99. The new public Make target passes with Python and uv blocked.

The unchanged independent portal peer moved from an example to `tests/support/global_shortcut_portal_peer.rs`, with Cargo fixture-binary metadata. Both native consumers use Cargo's actual executable path, removing their guessed debug/example directory. Its SHA-256 is unchanged: `b4f8f6b3ada9ed27130220352de792275a5cadbf21ae20ca9e55a9780f5a7709`. It is not shipped in the nine-executable runtime.

Before deleting `linux/tests/global_shortcut_portal_smoke.py`, its complete `exercise_private_portal` check, `SyntheticPortal` peer, shell/Make/CI callers, production owner and overlapping native comparisons were reviewed. It came from the released private-portal smoke work, including commits `905359c` and `19c7579`. It guarded host registration, the three proposed/approved shortcuts, held-key duplicate suppression, cancel/latest activation, compositor-trigger updates and closing the session. The stronger retained native owner compares **21 unchanged released workflows / 59 event states**, including exact request/cleanup traces, pending approval, rebinding, malformed/foreign responses, errors, caller disconnect and acknowledged shutdown. That existing owner replaces the 244-line Python helper; its protocol peer is reused rather than duplicated. Python unit tests and production shortcut code remain because the retained Python application still calls them.

The application-level consumer also passes all **eight released workflows / 34 GTK, preference, History, clipboard and independent-target states**, plus the pending-readiness key-change fault. It confirms exact-once replacement of a selected emoji, copy-only button capture, cancellation, key changes, rejected approval, provider repair, latest-conversation navigation and shutdown through the moved peer. Its synthetic audio and loopback speech endpoint remain private; these are not physical function-key or real microphone observations.
